subject: Counterfactually ablate one mesh message to measure whether communication added unique information

body.text: For one already completed mesh-triggered proof result, perform a bounded non-mutating replay from the same recorded coordination/canonical basis with exactly that external mesh event withheld. Ask whether the same WorkGraph obligation and materially equivalent evidence/result would have been derived from canonical state alone. If yes, classify the message as redundant coordination for that basis; if no, identify the smallest unique predicate/evidence edge the message contributed. Do this only where the basis is reproducible and cheap enough; never rewrite canonical history and never treat absence in a replay as proof of causal necessity beyond the bounded setup. Pair the ablation result with observed provider usage so we can learn when talking is useful versus when shared state should speak for itself. A good first candidate is the dual-key rendezvous or executable-baton work because both already produced concrete receipts.
